messages:
maya (PM): Quick sync — we need to pick an ordering for the inference perf work: reduce p99 tail latency, boost Dedicated throughput, and cut per-token cost with quantization/batching. Customer asks + launch criteria are sticky. thoughts?

arjun (Eng): Short: we can't do all at once. curious if we're using RICE or just impact/effort here.

maya (PM): leaning RICE for defendable ordering. impact = customer churn/usage uplift, reach = affected flows, confidence = data from spikes, effort = eng estimate.

samira (SRE): FYI, reducing p99 for hosted API affects our autoscale behaviour. Batching usually improves cost but can hurt tail latency unless we do adaptive timeouts.

lucas (ML): For quantization, we should run a compatibility matrix spike across models. Quality drop threshold we set at <2% on our eval pass; anything above needs QA sign-off.

olivia (Product-Eng): Customer ask: Platform team at Tremor (mid-market) sees high p99 spikes during peak search and said they'd consider Dedicated if we improve tail. That's immediate revenue signal.

arjun (Eng): Proposal: do a 2-week spike for quant + model eval (lucas), parallel 1-week effort to prototype adaptive batching (eng infra), then canary adaptive batching on 10% traffic to measure latency impact. If batching shows >10% tail regression, rollback.

lucas (ML): Agree. Spike plan: run quantization at 4/8-bit configs on representative models, measure eval score delta and token/sec. Also check runtime memory and KV-cache interactions.

maya (PM): Let's RICE-score quickly in-channel. I'll open a doc later but rough numbers now: p99 reduction -> Reach: 0.6, Impact: 8, Confidence: 0.6, Effort: 20 person-days. throughput -> Reach: 0.4, Impact: 5, Confidence: 0.5, Effort: 15pd. cost (quant+batch) -> Reach: 1.0, Impact: 6, Confidence: 0.5, Effort: 10pd.

arjun (Eng): Those effort numbers look optimistic for p99 work; add +30% for edge cases and rollout automation.

samira (SRE): Launch criteria we need to be explicit about: p99 < 200ms for short tokens path OR 30% reduction over baseline; throughput target: sustained tokens/sec at 95% of Dedicated SLA; cost: >=15% $/token reduction without quality regression.

olivia (Product-Eng): Sequencing suggestion based on revenue: 1) quant+batch spike (fast win, high reach), 2) adaptive batching canary (measure tradeoffs), 3) p99-specialized work (attention kernel optimizations) — because Tremor is willing to sign Dedicated only if p99 improves but quant improvements keep hosted adoption healthy.

arjun (Eng): Ok. I'll scope two stories: QUANT-SPIKE (10d), ADAPTIVE-BATCH-PROTOTYPE (7d) and P99-KERNEL-SPIKE (15d). Can we commit resourcing?

maya (PM): I'll propose that to Eng leads — aim to staff QUANT and BATCH first. Decision: run quant spike and adaptive batch prototype in parallel, canary batching at 10% for 72h if metrics look good. P99 kernel work to follow depending on canary and Tremor negotiations.

olivia (Product-Eng): I'll flag Tremor with a tentative timeline (3 weeks for spike + 1 week for canary).

deploy-bot: canary started on prod-cluster-3 (10% traffic) — QUANT-SPIKE and BATCH-PROTOTYPE running in staging.

samira (SRE): I'll watch p50/p95/p99 dashboards and alert if tail crosses thresholds.

arjun (Eng): ack. I'll post ticket numbers and rough story points to the roadmap doc.

maya (PM): thanks all — good sequencing. If any unexpected regressions, we revert canary and escalate. :thumbsup:
